# Chapter Twenty-Two: Wardens' Keep

Marcus awoke with a start, clearing his head he looked confused for a moment until he heard the low growl of the big cat that slept next to his tent. Stepping out he looked around and found Corliss standing a few feet away eyeing the animal. In her had was a small plate of meat, her eyes never left the ambers ones of the large white cat. “I was bringing you breakfast, apparently this one had objections” she said. Marcus smiled and laid a hand on the large beast, scratching the soft fur behind his head “easy boy, it’s food” he said and the growling ceased as the animal licked its chops and looked between the two, its eyes going from predator to begging and Marcus laughed, plucking a piece of the rabbit off of the plate he gently fed it to the large beast. Holding it out, the cat moved its head slowly and gently, almost daintily plucked the meat from his hand.

Nero took the plate with a thank you, Corliss turned to go but kept a suspicious eye on the large cat. “I don’t think she likes you” he said, and the cat switched its tail dismissively almost as if saying “Like I care”. Marcus just smiled again and handed the cat another piece of the steaming rabbit which it gobbled up greedily. “I am pretty much guessing this won’t do it for you.

Marcus closed his eyes, not sure if it was going to work but trying it anyway, he pictured hunting a deer and send it to the big cat. The animal regarded Marcus and then with a grunt rose from the ground and padded out into the woods. “Where is he going?” a voice came from behind him and he turned to find Dara, also carrying her own plate and walking over to join Marcus for breakfast. “I sent him out to find food” he answered shrugging Dara paused for a moment, brushing a lock of black hair out of her face as a small smile appeared and lit her face making her look young and vibrant. “You are going to feel really bad if he comes back carrying a farmer” she joked, and Marcus laughed motioning her to join him.

They sat eating in silence for a time, Marcus looking over the camp as Maelen and Patrice at near his tent and Corliss ate alone, the small group had made camp late the night before exhausted they had setup and quickly passed out. They were still days away from the capital and Marcus had no plan, no idea what he would do or what he would face but knew this was the right move.

He had been altered, even now he could feel the power flowing over and through the runes that had replaced a portion of his skin. No one else could stop the Empress and her chosen, the mages that now held the land hostage with there power and their guard dogs.

He would bring an end to this, bring an end to the slavery and death that this woman had brought to them.

“Are you okay?” Dara asked gently snapping Marcus out of his thoughts. It took him a moment before he nodded “Im okay” he said, knowing he wasn’t, he didn’t know if he would ever be again. The old mages words echoed through his mind “people fear what they don’t understand, if they know what you are capable of, they will fear you Marcus Gavin, you are something that has not walked this earth in generations”. The thought kept rolling over and over in his mind, the old mage was right, and Marcus knew it, knew what people would do if they found out how much power Marcus had at his fingertips.

Then there were the dreams, the thrumming from across the sea, something was calling out, calling to him he thought and whatever it was, would bring death and destruction with it he thought. “There you go again” Dara teased but he could hear the concern I her voice, he couldn’t hide his worry and his fear from her, she was very good at reading him, much like Orah had been he thought and a twinge of guilt flashed through his mind as he thought of the woman who had died, the woman who he had loved more then anything. “I will be fine” he simply answered but looking into her face he could see, she didn’t believe him, but she left it alone and with a mental thank you he went back to eating.

The large cat returned two hours later as the group packed the camp and prepared to head out.

The large animal came sauntering back into camp licking its chops and laid down next to Marcus with an audible grunt. Turning he regarded the cat and shook his head disapprovingly “Your late” he simply said, the cat yawning in disinterest as Marcus walked over setting the saddle on his back, trying to urge the animal to get up, which took longer then he would have liked but finally the big cat responded with a small chuff. “Don’t give me lip, you are the one who over ate and now thinks he needs a nap, we don’t have time” Marcus chided the cat, the large animal turned and licked his hand, Marcus smiled “apology accepted” he said scratching the back of his ear.

“What are you going to name him?” Corliss called saddling her own horse and smiling at Marcus, pausing he looked at the cat closely and then finally shook his head “I don’t know yet” he said and went back to packing the saddle bags and ensuring he had everything. Half an hour later the entire group was heading south towards the capital. They still had a long journey ahead of them and a lot of potential danger along the way he thought leading the group. They continued to ride for most of the day, staying away from villages and citys as best they could. It wasn’t until close to dusk that a rising commotion caught Marcus’s attention.

He stopped halting the group as he continued to listen, the sounds of shouting and screaming echoing over the wind and through the woods. Following the sound, he crept through the woods until he came to the outline of a large wall, one of the simple ones built to protect the medium size villages throughout the land. “Anyone know which village that is?” he called to the others as they stopped, studying the walls as they listened to the shouting and screaming coming from the other side. “Colrin, I think” Corliss called from the rear of the precession then she paused “Marcus, we shouldn’t” she finished, and he could hear the wince, knew what it took for her to give the assessment she just did.

Marcus nodded, knowing what she was saying, the more they stopped the more they interfered, the more likely the Empress would know they were coming. Marcus could not sit back while people suffered, he knew it was the wrong thing to do, but he could not turn away. Getting off of his tiger he stretched and began walking towards the entrance to the village. He could hear footsteps as the others did the same and he smiled a small smile. They had not even questioned him, his decision, they simply followed he knew that each of them did so not because he led, but because it was the right thing to do. Stepping to the gate he saw the two guards tense but before they could do much of anything, they both simply dropped to the ground, he could see they were still breathing and turned his head curiously. Dara stood there smiling, “A little something I learned” she shrugged still smiling.

Marcus would have to ask her to teach him that later he thought as he walked past the resting bodies of the guards. Stepping into the courtyard of the village he witnessed pure pandemonium as soldiers took children from screaming mothers, placing them into a large cage cart, they did this repeatedly as other guards pushed back the surge of villagers who stood incensed, angered. One man stood apart from the others yelling orders to the guards. “He is mine” Marcus said stepping forward and towards the scene playing out.

Marcus stood there watching the scene play out, the children pushed into the caged cart, crying as they reached out to there parents, scared as mothers screamed and begged the single man who stood giving the orders. He was almost aloof in his demeaner and after a few moments he finally noticed the small group regarding them. In his head he could hear the whisperes as options began playing out for him Marcus nodded to himself listening as various options laid out to him from the ages of knowledge now stored within him.

“Get them” came the voice of the leader as he pointed towards Marcus and the soldiers turned, half remaining with the crowd, the other half began moving in on the small group. “You don’t want to do this, lay down your weapons and surrender, you will be aloud to live” Marcus announced and he could hear the chuckle of the soldiers as they continued to move forwards, swords and guns out as they closed in. Marcus called forth the power and felt as it energized his system, flowed over his runes, like a drug the feeling was almost pure ecstasy. Reaching out he closed his hand and watched as the first ten guards simply crumpled too the ground, the sound of screaming and breaking bones emanating from their bodies. His smile grew wider as he focused on the next group but before he could do anything they dropped their weapons and began to claw at there throats, Marcus cocked his head and as he watched, their faces turned blue and they crumbled to the ground, looking at the figures lying on the ground he could see they were still breaking and turning he saw Maelen looking at him. The look on his face was anger and concern, He didn’t approve of Marcus’s methods he thought turning back to the group.

“Leave or die” he said simply tired of the games, tired of the violence. He had the power to simply kill these men to remove the stain of there existence from the world, they did not deserve to exist he thought and felt the power began to rise as did his anger until he felt the gentle hand on his shoulder, looking he could see Dara, the fear and the concern and something else he thought, almost like revulsion warred on her face. “Don’t” she whispered, and Marcus let the power go, dropping the building spell as his shoulders slumped as well.

He understood, he had almost slaughtered these men simply because he could. There was no thought to it, he was just going to kill the entire group without a second thought and Marcus took a shaky breath. His mind retreating at the thought of what he had almost done.

As he stood there Corliss and Maelen moved in, one of the guards raised the old musket and Corliss drilled him in the shoulder, he would live but he wouldn’t be firing a weapon anytime soon. “Listen up, drop your weapons, move away from the crowd, NOW” she said taking control of the situation as Marcus still tried to resolve what had almost happened, what he had almost done. Maelen stepped up as the leader began to pull a pistol from his own belt, before it could even clear the holster, he flicked his hand and the pistol, holster and most of the belt it was attached to flew off into the distance. “The lady said drop them” he followed up. The soldiers quickly realized they were dealing with not one but multiple mages, dropped weapons and began to move slowly away from the crowd. The people surging in and tearing open the caged cart, retrieving children and handing them back to the parents.

As the soldiers moved Corliss stepped over to the leader, with a well practiced motion she kicked the back of his knee bringing the large well-dressed man to his knees. “What was the plan?” she asked and waited, at first the man didn’t speak but a quick look towards Maelen and Marcus made the decision for him. “I don’t want any trouble especially with mages, I am just doing what I was told to, order came down to deliver the kids to the tower that is all I know, all the villages are doing it” he stammered cringing as he waited for the retribution to come. Grabbing him by the back of the neck she dragged him a few feet and threw him at the retreating soldiers “Take him too, leave” she said and two of the soldiers grabbed the leader, picking him up and taking him along, they walked out of the village, weapons left behind as the group made an exodus. Maelen gathered the villages, had them pick up the weapons. “We are heading to the capital to try and fix this, try and return this land to what it was, not what it is, protect yourselves until we do” he said and the men and women quickly picked up the weapons, one man stepping forward and began to coordinate guards and patrols.

Corliss and Maelen returned to where Marcus still stood, slumped shoulders and the defeated look on his face, he had almost slaughtered them, people following orders, soldiers and didn’t even give the decision a second thought. Grabbing him by th shoulder Maelen lead the young man out of the village, back out of the gate and towards the horses and his cat. “Marcus, something happened to you, the Silvan’s did something I can see that the way you handled the Seer’s, the power was like nothing I have ever seen. But now you have access to that power you need to remember that it is part of you, not in control of you.” He began turning the younger man to himself. “Remember who you are, you have the ability to kill with only a mere thought, I know you didn’t get the training that we put all mages through and its easy to allow something like the power you now possess to go to your head. Don’t let it control you Marcus, don’t let it take you over.” He finished and Marcus locked eyes with him he could see the other man’s pleading gaze, knew what he meant, knew what he was saying.

There was still a part that scoffed at it, told Marcus that he had the power, he now was the most powerful being on the planet and with that came the ability to rule these people because he was better than they were. With effort he pushed that down, that nagging voice, the one who told him he was destined to decide the fate of this world, the one who told him killing those less then he was, wasn’t murder, no more then stepping on an ant was. His own thoughts horrified him, where did this come from, why was it in his head he thought to himself. He wouldn’t admit it to anyone, much less those close to him, but he was fighting a battle and he didn’t know if he could win it, the cost would be his conscience, his humanity and losing those would make him no better then the Empress herself.

“Ill be okay” he simply said to Maelen, the other man looking at him, searching his face and looking for a truth he didn’t find. “I am having thoughts” he began and couldn’t go on, he couldn’t tell this man who he considered a friend and a mentor the things going through his head but he didn’t need to, Maelen nodded his eyes told him he understood, knew what he was going through. “You need to stay in control Marcus, you need to remember who you are, not give in to what you are” he said, squeezing the young man’s shoulder. Marcus nodded they stood there for a time the Runic mage pondering the thoughts that rolled through his mind as Maelen looked on, the concerned look not leaving his face.

Corliss and the others came out of the village a short time later. “Everything okay?” the Warden asked looking between Maelen and Marcus, he could see the look on Dara’s face as well. Whatever they saw on Maelen’s however told them it wasn’t a good time and with a nod they returned to the horses, the group heading out of the village. “The Empress is pulling the children, I don’t know why but she is having them sent to the tower, whatever it is, it cannot be good” Corliss said and Marcus could see his old mentor shiver, he had been at the tower, had seen first hand what happened there “If they are shipping them to the tower, then it is most definitely not good, we need to stop her and before she can enact whatever plan she has, we have maybe a week until the kids start arriving there” Marcus said and without prompting the group sped up a little, now they were on a clock.

As the sun began to set the group found a spot to camp for the night. Marcus sat alone as the others sat around the fire eating and talking, he ran his hands over the head of the large cat as he lay next to him napping. He had almost killed all those men today, his mind did not feel like his anymore he reflected the voice in his head urging him, taunting him, telling him to use his power to control those who were less. Where did this voice come from, he wondered as the cat vibrated a long low pur emitting from its sleeping form. Marcus smiled; he had never been a cat person but the beast had grown on him over the last few days and just as quickly the smile faltered the whispered returning, not like the ones that delivered the knowledge buried now in his head from the transfer, but another voice, another whisper one that told him he was better, stronger and destined to rule, that these people were primitive, simple and in need of guidance, the kind of guidance he could give them. With his power there was none who could stand against him. Closing his eyes, he willed the voice away. It had become stronger over the past few weeks emerging since the change that he had gone through at the hands of the Silvan’s. Marcus did not think the voice was tied to the transfer, if anything it had been there all along, thinking back to the whispers driving him to find answers, to drive him to use his power if anything it had only gotten louder, he surmised.

Marcus continued to pet the big cats head, the aforementioned snoring loudly to his personal amusement the young mage thought. “Can I join you?” came a familiar voice and he turned to find Dara standing there, a plate of food in her hand with a smile which even surprised him he reflected, in fact he was very happy she had come over that was something he would have to reflect on he thought motioning her over. “You are literally just a giant stomach aren’t you” Marcus said still scratching the large animals head. It shot him an annoyed look and then turned those soulful amber eyes to the woman with the plate. The large animal turned over onto its back and gently pawed the air at Dara “Oh, who is a big kittie” she cood at him, to which he shot me a look that said “see, someone appreciates me”.

Marcus shook his head “Suck up” he said to the cat, getting up to retrieve a plate from Dara. The raven-haired mage stooped down and pulling a piece of meat off her plate she held it out and the large cat gently took it, daintily eating the small morsel. Shaking his head Marcus dug into the food “So, are you okay?” Dara asked gently, Marcus looked into her eyes he could see the concern and something else he thought, something he knew very well, a look he himself had given to Orah. “I think I am, but there are moments.” he said trailing off as he looked away from her as he studied the woods.

“Marcus, I see you fighting with yourself, I saw what you almost did, something is going on” she said and he refused to look into those eyes, he was scared he wouldn’t be able to “I will be okay” he simply said mustering his will he looked into those concerned eyes and smiled in a way he hoped was reassuring. Dara dropped it nodding her head and concentrating on her food they both ate in silence eventually making small talk, but he could tell she was still worried, still concerned for him. Eventaully, mercifully they went to bed, Marcus crawling into the small tent and lying there thinking about the voice, about Dara and about the coming confrontation. Drifting off to sleep he thought about Orah and Dara and how he felt about the woman who so obviously cared for him, there was still guilt, but less then before he thought and spent the rest of his waking moments thinking about the Mage who loved him.

The next day was uneventful the group making good time towards the capital it wasn’t until evening was fast approaching that they came to the border of the Capital and into a waiting camp of soldiers. It took a moment to realize that the soldiers were not the Empress’s. Maelen sat forward in his saddle gawking as he studied the soldiers. “I didn’t think it was possible” he whispered looking as if he had seen a ghost. Marcus looked between his friend and the camp. “What is it Maelen?” he asked confused as he tried to ascertain the man’s shock. “The soldiers, are, of Aurtus.” he said, and the tone of his voice held fear.

Marcus looked confused for a moment “Whats wrong?” he asked the hackles on his neck going up as Maelen rode forward to come sit next to the young mage. “The mage wars, this is the church’s army Marcus, the one that hunted Zathris until the inception of the agreement” he whispered. Marcus got it; it would be like seeing a Nazi army in the 80’s he thought getting down off the cat. “Stay here” he said to the group, Corliss was already getting down “Not going in along Marcus” she said the others obeyed. Marcus did not need old wounds causing problems, he had to find out why they were here. Marcus took a breath and eyed the soldiers who eyed them. They didn’t seem hostile, but they weren’t friendly either he noticed. The wary looks he got told him they recognized the style of dress; they knew he was a mage and not a one of them was happy about it.

“This is ought to be good” he whispered looking at the preparations the soldiers were making, they were preparing for war. Wading through the sea of bodies, his eyes caught the armor and the designs, they wore runic armor, something he thought only mages wore, the weapons too had runs carved into the blades and bows. This army, if history was to be believed were Mage killers, the weapons and armor would allow them to fight those who use magic as a weapon he reflected.

A part of him wanted to test this, to test the runes against his own magic, but if it were detected, they would not be a good way to start a conversation. So, he continued forward, seeing the large tent in the middle of the sea of soldiers, he aimed for it. The soldiers though watching him did not move to stop either of them. They moved with a purpose, finally reaching the large tent, the fabric was new meaning it had not been up that long, still white with creases in it from being stored and folded. The wood pegs were all newly cut, whoever this army was they had not been here for long. Approaching the door, the two guards on either side of the entrance moved into their way “Halt” one said and the two came up short, waiting for the next inevitable questions. “Who are you, what is your business here Mage” he said and the way he said mage left very little interpretation as to how he felt about them. “I am here to see your leader” Marcus answered looking bored as his eyes roved the camp, purposely avoiding the guards as if they were of little concern.

He had known his share of officers, knew how to make someone feel unimportant and decided to go with this tact, as if he were here for a meeting and anyone else other then the person, he was meeting with were mere functionaries. One of the guards nodded to the other and entered the tent, Marcus could hear the light murmuring as he announced their presence, he hid a smile knowing the man was at a loss for who was outside since he hadn’t asked.

The curtain parted and the guard nodded to them “You may enter” he said and moved allowing the two entry into the tent. Marcus stepped in to see a Soldier and another man, a young man dressed in an ornate armor, one with the emblazoned Aurtus sitting on a throne across his chest. Corliss cocked her head “I know you, you’re the messenger we took to the old Warden’s complex” she said with a half smile looking the man over. The ornately dressed man looked up at the Warden.

“Yes Warden Corliss, I know very well who you are and what you have done” he began and then his eyes fell on Marcus and the smile quickly disappeared “In fact that was the only reason you were aloud entry, how is it you travel with a mage might I ask” he continued the word mage sounding more like a disease then a title. Marcus stood silent sensing it was probably best to allow the Warden to do the talking. “We have come to confront the Empress” she said and before she could continue the man held up his hand, the look on his face was firm and the gesture not kind, it was a command.

“Warden you and the mage will stand down, this is our battle, we are here to remove the Empress from power and take control of Vicor, to restore the country and bring it back from this nightmare” he said and before either one could protest. “This is not a request, this is my order, if you involve yourself, you will be considered an enemy, stand down and watch if you must but stay out of it” he finished and the two stood there astounded for a moment, The Warden nodded “Of course, however should you need us we will be here” she simply said and nudging Marcus they two left the tent.

“What the hell are we doing?” Marcus hissed once they were out of earshot and on their way back to the group. The group had now become surrounded by soldiers as they eyed them suspiciously. “Can’t you see, they don’t trust mages right now, if you give them an excuse they will arrest you and them or worse, lets just stand by, I have a feeling we will be needed” she said as they finally reached the group.

They turned and rode a good distance from the camp and setup their own, allowing them a good vantage point of the battlefield. Marcus filled in the group and everyone seemed stunned in fact Maelen looked as if someone had punched him in the gut. “This is not good Marcus, this is not good at all, if they have decided the agreement has been broken, it could mean bad things for all Mages” he whispered. His eyes intent but looking at the camp and not at anyone there.

The small group sat around the fire as the sun set, they had spent the day watching the preparations for the morning. They obviously planned to go in the following day “So I have a few questions” Dara began still looking down the hill towards the large campsite. “Why are we just sitting here and why would the Empress allow a standing army to setup within only a few miles of the capital” she queried finally turning back to the group. “The answer to question one is because if we try to push, they will quite probably arrest us, they are clearly not fans of mages right now and with all that has happened, I can’t blame them, second because she too needs to gather her soldiers, I don’t know what she has in the capital but it can’t be a lot” Corliss said staring into the fire as the flames began to dance to the light gust of wind.

The group sat in a morose silence, having come so far to be sidelined by of all things the church, but Maelen seemed far more bothered by this then the others. “Maelen, whats wrong?” Marcus inquired taking his eyes from the flames. He could see the haunted look in his friends’ eyes as he stared down upon the sea of tents gathered below them. “Once those people hunted us down like dogs, it was only Zathris and his ability to bring us together that saved Mages, but that was at a time when we were more powerful then we are today Marcus, if the church has decided we have broken the agreement, then we will be hunted down like dogs, tortured for information leading to others, it will be a horror to end all horrors my friend” he said.

Marcus listened as the whispered agreed with his friend. His knew knowledge of history flashed through his mind, the torture and the horror as written by those where there if the church came to the conclusion that the mages had broken the agreement then what would happen next would be worse by an order of magnitude then what the Empress had just put this country through.

They slept fitfully Marcus spying the guards that lined the edge of the camp, watching them, after the conversation the night before the guards were unsettling and no one slept well. Morning came with a flurry of activity as the soldiers mustered, waking the small camp as Marcus crawled from his small tent to see the sea of soldiers resplendent in armor standing as they faced towards the capital. Lord Regeant Juric Nero rode along the front line, yelling to his men as they began to beat the runic shields in time. The sea of men began to move forward marching in time towards the silhouette of the capital.

Out of the corner of his eye Corliss moved, reaching into her bag and pulling out a piece of leather with two polished glass lenses, after a moment of carefully assembling it with purposeful and practiced moves, she brought it up to her eye, pushing a strand of blonde hair out of her face. He watched as she grimaced “The Empress and her soldiers are on the move” she said and then handed the device to Marcus.

He looked it over, understanding at once he was looking at an early version of a monocular and smiling, he rose it to his eye and pointed it towards the silhouette of the capital. He could see the soldiers pouring out of the gate, already in motion towards the line of Aurtus’s army. Upon the ramparts stood three figured the center one was the Empress he assumed as the two shadowy cloaked figures bookending her were definitely seers. “Rogan” Marcus growled as the hoods came down and he could see the bruises and scrapes, but it was definitely the one who had gotten away. “She is protected by mages; they won’t get near her” he finished stating the obvious as the woman on the ramparts watched smiling as the soldiers continued to pour forth from the capital.

Marcus gently handing the monocular to Dara their hands touching for only a moment as a small shock jumped between them, He looked into those dark eyes and saw the twinkle as a smile spread across her face. Her stare lingered for only a moment and then brought the device to her face, her smile quickly disappearing as she scanned the capital walls “Screamers” she whispered and handed it back to Marcus, he quickly looked and with Dara guiding the Monocular he saw what she had and inhaled a quick intake of breath. “How are there so many” he said remembering the twenty who had escaped, but there were more then a hundred of the creatures swarming over the walls and sliding onto the battlefield. They moved onto the field and Marcus handed the device to the waiting hands of Maelen. Patrice still sat by the fire looking at the group and Marcus could see the concern and worry on her face as she stared at Maelen, who for his part purposely avoided making eye contact. He could imagine what she was thinking, she had almost lost him, thought him dead and he had come back to her. Now here he was putting himself right back in danger, her not joining them was a silent protest, she wanted Maelen safe, wanted him to sit this one out but knew damn well he wouldn’t, he couldn’t. So instead she removed herself, refusing to take part in something that once again put her lover’s life in danger.

“We need to get into this fight” He said as if stating it despite Patrice’s feeling on the subject. Marcus looked between the two and could feel the heat of Patrice’s look as it radiated against the back of Maelen’s neck. “We sit it out for now, but keep ready, we might need to come in to turn the tide, I don’t think they know what they are getting into” Marcus said, turning back to watch the fight as the two armies careened towards each other with murder in their eyes. “We can’t just sit here, they will be slaughtered” Dara said and Marcus turned seeing the worry and fear in the eyes of the mage, putting a hand on her shoulder he squeezed, bringing her eyes to meet his “If we get into the middle of this without an invitation, I have the feeling we will be the enemy as well Dara, don’t worry, we will get into this” he vowed, his eyes breaking contact to look towards the tent where the new Lord Regent now stood planning with his military staff.

Rogan was on the ramparts, the screamers were on the field and the Empress herself had not left the castle, this was for keeps he thought, today would decide the fate of all of Vicor. The soldiers began to pick up page as the field in between the two armies shortened and then the sky turned black as arrows shot up from each sight, so many arrows Marcus thought as the sun was blocked out and the arrows fly up, arcing through the sky and began there deadly descent. Soldiers dropped on both sides as they found their home, those not lucky or quick enough dropping to the ground most with mortal wounds.

Then the two groups clashed a cacophony of metal against metal as sword met shield and the deadly art of swordfighting began. Marcus looked on watching as mundane fought mundane, this was not the fight he was worried about, his eyes roved over the field as the soldiers hacked at each other, he concentrated trying to find.. and then a small flash of light as he found one of the screamers, it had hopped upon a soldier and its claws was tearing into the man’s neck, stopping every so often to throw fire and electricity in the direction of his friends. Watching his eyes went wide was it possible he thought waiting to see it again and looking closely he saw the screamer throw fire at one of the Aurtus soldiers, the blaze hitting the front of the armor and being absorbed, he watched the runes glow across the chestplate and the flame’s power flowing through the armor down into the arm, as he continued to watch the soldier’s sword erupted into fire, the power transferring to the weapon and powering the spell. “How is that possible” he whispered watching as it attacked the creature, slashing at its body and head, it only took moments as the surprised creature fell, headless to the ground and the blade dimmed as the power ebbed. Maelen cursed “They have found the armor of Aurtus” he said his voice sounded disgusted as they continued to watch. Marcus heard the whispers as they explained the comment, but Dara did not share that gift and looked curiously at Maelen. “What is that?” she asked watching as another Screamer fell to the magic weapons of the church’s soldiers.

Turning to the group he nodded to the field “During the mage wars the church hired mages that had remained neutral during the war, these men were experts in runic script, not only understanding it but like Marcus sharing that same close relationship with the power giving them the ability to see it. The mages discovered that by combining the right runic symbols, they could create a spell that would absorb power and then using that power give the attack’s properties to the weapons or armor” he started, looking back to the soldiers his eyes roving over them as they pressed the attack. “It was the turning point of the war, until that moment, the only way to kill a mage usually ended in the death of up to ten of the soldiers, this somewhat leveled the playing field” Maelen finished. Dara looked out across the field and then back to the group “Who did they find to do it now and how did they get so much of it?” she queried, the question was innocent but it represented a disturbing realization but one that Maelen quickly brought to a close. “They didn’t, at least I don’t think they did. The armor and weapons they carry are of a very old style, I am guessing they stored the original armor someplace after the end of the War, in case it would be needed” he surmised, and Marcus winced. That would mean the church had a plan in place should the mages break the agreement, should they once again attack he thought.

Looking over the field he thought back to the look on the Lord Regent’s face, the man hated Marcus, hated what he was and what he represented, it was very possible the church had already decided the mages had indeed broke the agreement. If that was the case then it was also possible that they would hunt down any they suspected of crossing the line, of using their powers against mundane’s he reflected. The group stood in silence thinking on this as they watched the battle from the hill, it was obvious the tide was turning, the Empress’s people were being beaten back, the screamers killed one after another. The church had their own losses, but they were definitely far fewer then those of the Empress’s men.

Despite the state of the battle, despite the death after death of the Empress’s troops, they did not retreat, did not regroup, they pressed forward, sometimes as pairs and sometimes alone. She was simply throwing there lives away in an effort to tire out the church’s own soldiers.

If that was the plan thought Marcus then there was another string to this bow, the Empress had a surprise and he began to look over the field, she was not stupid, in fact the woman was a cunning strategist, a brilliant planner, she would not stand there unless she was sure that her people could take the day, that she had the upper hand. “Maelen, what is the Empress planning, there is no way she is just going to let them capture her” Marcus said, eyeing the woman suspiciously from across the field.

They continued to watch the battle, the Soldiers for Aurtus pushed the Empress’s protectorate back further leaving bodies strewn across the field, the Empress’s soldiers did not run, did not turn but instead fought desperately each one until the death. The Screamers had been routed, the few left had returned to the wall of the castle perched there awaiting orders from the Empress. Standing there the woman simply waited, watching silently as the soldiers moved further and further forward until only a few were left, standing in front of the gate to the capital ready to defend it with there lives. Marcus noticed movement in the camp and spied the glint of armor as the Lord Regent moved from his tent and mounted his horse. “Its time” Marcus said and moving with a purpose he headed for his Cat, the others quickly finding the horses and mounting up, they rode quickly catching up with the Lord Regent as he entered the field of battle.

A small contingent of troops surrounding him for protection. “If you don’t mind Lord Regent, may we ride with you” Corliss said before Marcus could speak. The soldiers eyed the mages with hostility in their eyes, as if at any moment they would launch themselves from there horses and attack. Most had moved back as the large white tiger made its way alongside, walking with the group, its amber eyes flashing as it regarded the tender morsels in funny bright wrappers. Marcus could see the fear in every pair of eyes that regarded them. The large cat licked its lips slowly and glared back, rolling his eyes and suppressing a smile Marcus cuffed the large cat on the head lightly “knock it off” he whispered and the cat looked away everything about his movements unconcerned with the soldiers.

Nero looked at the group, paying particular attention to the mages. “Warden Corliss, because of your aid and your good will towards myself and the people of Vicor, I will allow it, however you are responsible for the actions of the mages, I trust you can keep them in line” he said and Maelen laid a hand on Dara’s arm before she could launch into the argument that had come to her lips. If eyes could kill, hers would be shoot daggers at the Lord Regent, but she kept quiet and instead choosing simply to stay silent and look forward. But Marcus could see the tight line of her jaw as she held her tongue.

Corliss smiled easily at the Lord Regent and with a slight bow spoke “Of course Lord Regent Nero, I will be responsible for there actions, I appreciate you allowing us to accompany you” she finished and fell back to ride with the group. “He has settled into the role of pompous ass nicely” She whispered as she came along side the mages. She eyed Dara for a moment “That was calculated, he was trying to get a rise out of you, any excuse to remove us from his presence” she said her tone fairly neutral, but her eyes said otherwise, she regarded Dara cooly at first and then warmed, smiling at the young mage “I get it, he is an ass, don’t let him get to you” she said gently.

She turned her attention to Marcus who sat up in his saddle, back rigid as he continued to eye the Empress. “Whats wrong Marcus, you look like your ready for something to jump out of the shadows at any moment.” She asked giving him a concerned look. “Every fiber in my head, and let’s just say in my experience, this is not like the Empress, she has something planned. I am just not sure what it is, lets keep our eyes open guys” he said, and everyone nodded.

The small group rode across the field, avoiding the bodies upon bodies that lay there, some the Empress’s and some the Lord Regents, but all young men, fighting for there betters and paying the ultimate price Marcus thought looking down at them. He had seen men die, had seen war and no matter where in time it is, it was always the same, those without power paid the price for those with it.

Finally, the Lord Regent and his security contingent reached the gate, standing behind his men who stood threatenly towards the large wall and the few soldiers left.

Standing above them in her royal burgundy robes the Empress stood there, her blonde hair reflecting the sunlight of the day as she looked down upon the group, her eyes came to rest upon Marcus and smiled slightly as Rogan standing next to her nodded as her eyes moved to him. “Mage, I am glad you are here, it will save me having to find you when I am done here, I had wished for you to join me of your own volition, but that is of little consequence, you will join me reguardless” she said to Marcus. Nero shot a glance at him and then with irritation that was barely contained, addressed the Empress. “You are beaten my lady, there will be no later, you will surrender now and be taken into custody until such time the church can render a verdict for your actions. You have lost” he announced standing high in his saddle.

They ignored the Lord Regent for a moment, looking over the others in the group “You are mages, you should be standing with me, not this primped Messenger who fancies himself a leader” she began and then shot a hostile look at Nero himself “Pretty armor does not make you worthy of the title of Lord Regent, nor does it make you worthy of armor once worn by Tokimada himself Messenger, you disgrace him with every movement in it.” She spat at the Lord Regent.

Nero was about to launch into another round of announcements proclaiming her surrender when her hand shot up silencing him. “You have no idea who you are standing before or what you have gotten yourself in Messenger, the last time I saw that armor I stood right down there” she pointed to the middle of the field “General Tokimada of the Protectorate of Aurtus and Mage Zathris and myself stood there surrounded by mages and mundanes as the man humiliated us, forced us to sign your agreement, forced mages to stand down, to give up our destiny” she began and Nero laughed, but there was something in that laugh Marcus thought and he noticed Maelen who had turned sheet white. “Whats wrong?” Marcus whispered. The Empress was obviously mad he thought, he knew the story understood of when she was talking but that was nearly a thousand years ago, it would be impossible for her to have been there he thought, but something in Maelen’s face sent an alarm through him.

“It can’t be” Maelen said shaking his head as the Empress eyed him and smiled. “That’s right old man, I am Eleneaor, Commander of the red army, the knights of magic who once almost conquered this land, almost united this continent as one to ensure our survival until Tokimada joined forces with Zathris, the man he had been trying to hunt and kill for so long.” The Empress paused, surveying the field as if seeing something from long ago, her face looked bitter as she continued.

“I was beaten, Tokimada had his mage armor and Zathris and his Runic Knights had beaten back my people, killed my generals, leaving me beaten on the field of battle, I signed the agreement, vowing one day to take what was rightfully mine” she proclaimed. At first only silence then laughter as Nero threw his head back “Woman, you are mad Eleneaor has been dead for nearly a thousand years, surrender now and I may show mercy” he spat. But the woman only stood there regarding him cooly for a moment.

Reaching her hands up she unclipped the burgundy robe allowing it to fall. Underneath she stood in black mage armor runes running over every piece of the black leather and barely noticeable, upon her hip sat the small obsidian staff, the mages weapon looking very much like that of Rogan’s or even Marcus’s he thought. “Enough games, it is time this ends” she said and with a nod both of the robe’s figures threw off their robes. The guards realized the threat, but a moment too late as the crossbows snapped up and fired, the mages knew already they could not affect the flight path of the runed bolt’s so pieces of the wall itself quickly put themselves in the path of them. With a small spark the six bolts careened away harmlessly.

Marcus felt the power as the Empress began to gather it, his eyes went wide as with his power he could see the power course through the familiar runic script running over her body, the same runic script that ran over hers. She knew how to alter her chosen, not because she had gotten a book or learned a long-lost secret he thought. But because she had been there, had it done to her, this mage was over a thousand years old and somehow had managed to stay alive he thought amazed. Before he could react, before he could defend the group the Empress unleashed the kinetic force of her blast. The soldiers had been protected against the sheer power, there runes absorbing it, but the front wall of the capital hadn’t, and large stone blocks shot out impacting the soldiers and carrying them backward over a hundred feet, all of them coming to land. Marcus might have been distracted but Maelen had not been, the stones smacked into a shield and the entire group was forced backward, no one was hurt, however.

Once they stopped he looked over at the pile of bodies as the Lord Regent slowly got up unsteadily to his feet, blood covered half his face as he rocked back and forth, his face dazed from the block that had slammed into his face. Marcus could see the odd way his jaw sat, the block had smashed it, but the man was in shock and wouldn’t feel it for a little bit he thought. The Empress laughed and pointed at Nero. “You think because you wear that pathetic armor you are safe from me little priest, think again” she said and power erupted from her fingertips as flames slammed into Nero’s face. His screams could be heard even over the roar of fire. Patrice was moving even as the fire left the Empress’s fingers.

With a blast of force she picked up one of the fallen stones and slamming it into the Lord Regent she knocked him out of the way, extending her powers, she extinguished the fire and Marcus watched in awe as her fingers moved fast, weaving power over the burnt flesh, trying desperately to save the man’s life, the man who despised her simply because she had been born different. The doctor had not even hesitated and had left herself exposed. Marcus drew on his own power, feeling the runes begin to warn as he quickly slammed a shield in place just before electricity began to dance over it Rogan grinning viciously as he fingers moved caressing the shield. With his cowl drawn Marcus could see the weak pallor of his skin and sunken eyes the words of the Ancient Silvan mage jumped into his mind “The runs, if they are not done correctly will eat away at the mage” and it had, the man looked like he was barely holding himself together.

That did not mean he would show this animal mercy, flicking his hand the worn and haggard Seer launched backward from the wall, the sound of ribs breaking as the kinetic force of the spell slamed into him. A scream erupted from the Empress as she launched herself from the wall, hand slamming down as the stones shattered from the force of the spell as she launched over the group and out into the field. Marcus pushed his hand down and felt the power lift him as he launched after her. She was not getting away he vowed turning in mid air and shouting down to Maelen “Watch Patrice” he yelled.

Marcus arced up into the air but before he turned he caught sight of Corliss her fingers quickly dancing long the worn brown leather of the holsters low on her hips, without even a pause she grasped the sandalwood grips on the slender gold pistols and with a well practiced flick of her wrists they jumped out of the holsters flipping end over end in another well practice maneuver as the hammers slide between her thumb and forefinger two audible clicks sounding as they engaged in unision. Blue energy and crystal slugs erupted from the barrels slamming into the remaining Lord Seer as he began to leap from the wall, as if a giant had swatted the man he careened backward hitting the ground with a loud grunt of pain. “Go, I got this” she shouted as Marcus turned to face the ancient General who was Empress.

Marcus landed lithely upon the battlefield only feet from the woman who stood there, feet spread apart and weapon drawn. Eyeing the mages staff in her hand he drew his own, keeping it low on his thigh he slowly began to circle the woman, the first time these two had come face to face, this woman was responsible for so much pain in his life, she had hunted him relentlessly since he had landed upon this world. He regarded her cooly looking at this woman, this monster but she wasn’t a monster he thought, in fact she looked quite young and beautiful. The Empress stood there in the same armor, with the same weapon regarding this man who she had for so long sought.

“You are on the wrong side Mage, you should be sided with me” she simply said, though the weapon was out, she made no move to use it, merely turned to ensure she faced Marcus. “So, how is it you are still alive, I mean obviously magic, but how” he asked both changing the subject and getting to the heart of the matter. At first, she didn’t speak, just turning and smiling at him Marcus was about to ask again when she finally spoke. “There is no secret Marcus, it is not supernatural, After the wars Zathris decided that he could not leave me free so made a decision. Like you he landed late, came into this world after the others but he kept his pod, once the agreement had been signed he and a few of the Knights from his newly minted order placed me in his pod, putting me to sleep and then burying me, Ironically enough a malfunction released me over a decade ago” she said looking back towards the group as they continued to fight with what remained of her guard and the final Lord Seer.

Then she stopped Marcus cold in his tracks “Have you had the dreams Marcus, have you heard the thrumming from across the waters?” she asked, and he turned towards her. “Most cannot, but I see you do, something is coming and it means to destroy us, this is why I did what I did, this is why we, not the mundane’s need to rule Marcus, don’t you see, they are incapable of ruling themselves, they don’t know whats coming nor could they quit the political infighting long enough to solve it.” She continued and Marcus looked up his face hard.

“Your way was wrong; you are a monster and I will finish what Zathris should have done all those years ago” but she had anticipated his response and before he had even finished his sentence a bolt of power struck him throwing the young mage off his feet. Striking the ground, he looked up to see Victoria arcing through the air her mage staff separated as the two blades extended towards him.

Throwing power to his left his body slid out of the way, just in time to feel the air from the blades as they thrust into the ground. Flicking energy back the way he had come Victora’s legs went out from under her as the kinetic force hit them, dropping her to the ground. Marcus was up dropping force against the ground to bring him to his feet. He pulled his small stave apart, flipping it to show the crystal tipped ends as he threw fire and force at the other mage.

Even on the ground she was quick, using the runes in the staff to deflect away each attack. Marcus continued to throw attack after attack slamming the stave into the air as energy flew from the crystal, he could feel the river of power flowing from his arm and into the stave and using the runes across the side and the crystal to focus the attacks. Victoria parried another set of attacks, planting her hand on the ground she flew into the air leaving Marcus to scramble trying to follow the woman throwing attacks that missed. Coming down on her feet she blocked electric strands as they danced across her armor and stave.

Marcus pressed further, pushing more energy throwing attack after attack, but he was not as experienced as the Empress and she managed to throw fire hitting Marcus high in the leg, interrupting his casting long enough to get the upper hand. A blast of kinetic force took him off his feet as he felt two of his ribs shatter pain screaming up his side. Bringing his elbow out he used it to land, causing pain to lance up his arm, but much less he knew then if he had landed on his side.

Marcus Parried another three attacks and then threw up a shield, she was fast, faster than he was. He could see the runes play over her body as she threw spell after spell. Like him, her runes had been done by the Silvans ages ago, her ability to throw power was at his level, he would never be able to beat her with force and he knew it. Fire landed against his shield pushing him back with the sheer force of the spell.

Marcus could see the malicious smile lit by the aura of the fire “You cannot beat me young mage, I will destroy you and then destroy your friends, when I am done with the Lord Regent I will rebuild my army and ensure the safety of humanity once I have taken control of the Silvan empire, that old mage in the catacombs will create my next chosen, they will be perfect” she said the smile still on her face as she poured even more fire against his shield. He strengthened his own shield as flames began to lick around the edges, he could feel the heat and it was causing sweat to pour down his forehead.

“You can’t win this Victoria” he said but his voice was out of breath, weak and the Empress could sense it, her smile widened as they continued the battle of power. Marcus could feel his runes heating, could feel the sheer amount of power as he poured it into the shield, the fire eating it away the second it came into being. He could not hold this up indefinitely and both of them knew it as Victoria pushed harder, pouring enough power to melt rock.

“You will die here Mage, you will die here and so will your friends, I had thought you were the answer to my problems a Mage with enough power to power the next generation of my screamers but its obvious you are not the one, you are weak” she said taking a step forward as more power erupted from the two ends of the weapon. Marcus frantically looked around, trying to find something, anything he could to interrupt her, to stop her even if for only a moment. His skin was getting hotter as he pushed more power to the shield trying to counter the sheer heat of Victoria’s attack. A glint caught his eye a lone crossbow bolt sat upon the ground. Reaching out he almost kicked himself, it didn’t move, of course not he thought, he could see the runes light and expel the energy he had pushed at the bolt. Closing his eyes, he cursed and then opening them again he watched as the runes began to fade and then he noticed it.

Shifting as his skin heated even further, he extended two fingers and gently pulling at the bolt he concentrated on the fletching and a small smile crossed his mouth despite the discomfort and heat as it rose off the ground. Hands shaking from the strain of doing both he gently moved his fingers orienting the bolt. He felt the energy within him ebb, felt the shield as it began to fail, Victoria sensed it to, stepping forward once again she pushed even more energy into the spell and marcus could see the smoke rising from the armor as her own runes heated from the effort.

With what little energy he had left he pushed at the bolt sending it flying straight towards the Empress. A moment later the smile was replaced by a surprised and pained look as the bolt slammed home driving itself into her side. The spell fell apart and the fire vanished as Victoria dropped to her knees, reaching over with a shaky hand to feel the end of the deeply embedded shaft. “What have you done” she whispered as Marcus slowly rose from the ground. Every movement hurting as his own Armor smoked, he wasn’t sure how much damage he had done to his skin or the runes, but he knew he would have to examine them and soon.

Standing over the Empress he regarded her, faces came to him as he remembered the people hanging from walls or lying in gutters like yesterday’s garbage.

He would not make the same mistake that Zathris had, he wouldn’t leave her alive to do this again at some later time. Wincing as he drew upon the power the Empress smiled up at him “What?” he asked right before the tearing of stone and the screaming began. Marcus turned and looked in horror as two Metal giants climbed through the capital wall “did you think you were the only one who knew the secret of the metal sentries” she wheezed blood trickling down her chin as she continued to smile.

Marcus had no time, power flew as the others attacked the creatures, but they would be no match and he knew it. He glanced back at the Empress, the smug look on her face almost made him pause, almost made him finish the woman who had brought so much pain and death, but his friends needed him. Wincing in anticipation of the pain he slammed his hand towards the ground and rocketed back towards the wall. The group had decimated the final soldiers and with no small pleasure he spotted Rogan’s broken body lying behind the wall as he reached the pinnacle of his arc and then he began to descend.

He could see Corliss and Maelen standing their ground as the Lord Regent and what was left of his protective guard huddled behind them. Corliss’s gun and Maelen’s magic was joined by Dara and Patrice on the opposite side but it was having little effect. These were constructs, made of magic. As he flew through the air looking at the large human like constructs that lumbered slowly towards his friends something about that statement caught his attention Made of magic he thought again. Then he watched as Maelen threw lighting at the closest one and its body lit as Runes covering most of its body lit up mitigating the magic and absorbing it. Marcus read the lines and contours of the runes, but he wasn’t fast enough he got the basics and if he was right. “Hit him again” Marcus yelled down to his friend and mentor Maelen looked at him not knowing why but after a moment his face set in determination that Marcus knew what he was doing and hit the creature again, lighting dancing over its body and the runs lighting again.

Marcus extended his hand and changed his flight bringing him across the front but still out of reach of the creature. He watched the contours of power flowing over the runes, he didn’t have a lot of time the closest of the constructs was quickly approaching the small group of his friends. Passing across the front of the creature he spotted it. “This is going to suck” he whispered slamming his hand back sending himself careening towards the creature, he pulled his weapon apart brandishing the rune encrusted dagger. The construct sensed him but was too late as Marcus landed on its shoulder and slammed the blade of the dagger into a rune just to the right of its large metal neck. Power erupted from the rune slamming into Marcus and sending him flying.

He flew backwards dazed as he hit the ground knocking the air of out him. Everything seem to slow, he tried to get up, there was still one creature up as the first one fell first to its knees and then crumbled into a heap in front of his friends. The second one did not even slow, it kept moving forward the three mages throwing fire and electricity at the creatures with little effect. Marcus tried to yell, tried to tell them that magic wouldn’t work, that the rune was the key, but nothing but a long wheeze escaped his lips.

Then he saw her, Corliss running up a fallen tree and onto the rampart edge as she turned and sprinted towards the creature, her hands reaching behind her and producing a pair of black hatchets she launched herself from the wall and flew towards the back of the large construct as she landed on its back both of the hatchets drove into the creatures shoulders and light and energy erupted from them, but she had anticipated this and crouched below the blast, riding the creature to the ground as it landed next to its brother. Marcus rose nodding to Corliss; she had seen what he had done and understood it. The group stood there surveying the damage and Marcus turned back to the field but it was empty, the Empress was no longer there, snapping his head back towards the wall Rogan also was no longer lying on the ground. Both had used the distraction of the constructs to disappear.

Marcus could hear the dull thud of footsteps and turned to find a hundred soldiers spears pointed in their direction standing there. “Stand Down” came a voice and Marcus turned to see the Lord Regent, scarred armor but no worse for wear limping from the group where Maelen, Dara, Patrice and Corliss had protected him. Regent Nero eyed Marcus as he passed, without a word he simply nodded and continued on to the soldiers. Marcus didn’t care about the damn regent he turned to regard his friends, everyone was alive and with a smile he walked the few steps and threw his arms around Dara and Maelen “It’s done” he said and he could feel Maelen tense, letting him go he regarded his friend.

“Where is the Empress?” he asked, and Marcus shook his head “That’s for another day my friend”.
